research_mode: official MHCLG and ONS primary sources only; latest England fire-and-rescue statistics, CSEW quality/methodology and crime-statistics user-guide gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire and rescue statistics quarterly-release scope
verified_claims: The March 2026 fire and rescue incident statistics release is published quarterly and applies to England
limitations: a quarterly statistical release is not a real-time incident feed

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: IRS to FaRDaP collection transition
verified_claims: fire data were collected through the Incident Recording System until November 2025 and through the Fire and Rescue Data Platform from November 2025
limitations: the collection-system transition must be retained when comparing periods across November 2025

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire release coverage dimensions
verified_claims: the release covers incidents, fire-related fatalities, non-fatal casualties and response times for fire and rescue services in England
limitations: the release provides service and incident statistics, not parcel-level safety determinations

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire service incident-category framework
verified_claims: incidents attended by fire and rescue services are categorised as fires, non-fire incidents and fire false alarms
limitations: category totals and rounded shares must not be interpreted as property-specific risk

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Year ending March 2026 incident total
verified_claims: fire and rescue services attended 641,227 incidents in the year ending March 2026, including 170,597 fires
limitations: national annual totals cannot establish local or parcel exposure

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Year ending March 2026 fire-fatality total
verified_claims: there were 254 fire-related fatalities in 239 fatal fires in the year ending March 2026
limitations: small annual fatality counts are prone to fluctuation and later revision

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Incident-type share gate
verified_claims: fires accounted for 27%, fire false alarms 40% and non-fire incidents 34% of attended incidents in the year ending March 2026
limitations: published percentages are rounded and must not be forced to sum exactly

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Ten-year fire-service incident trend
verified_claims: total incidents increased by 21% between the years ending March 2016 and March 2026
limitations: the trend is descriptive and does not establish a causal driver

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Incident-composition shift
verified_claims: the share of non-fire incidents has increased while the share of fire incidents has decreased over the long term
limitations: a changing service mix does not by itself indicate changing parcel safety

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Suffolk submission-underestimate caveat
verified_claims: Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service could not submit all incidents between September 2024 and June 2025 for technical reasons
limitations: Suffolk figures for that period are an underestimate and should not be compared without the caveat

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Primary-fire classification definition
verified_claims: a primary fire meets at least one criterion involving a non-derelict structure or vehicle, a fatality casualty or rescue, or attendance by five or more pumping appliances
limitations: the classification is an incident-recording rule and not a continuous severity score

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Secondary-fire classification definition
verified_claims: secondary fires are generally small outdoor fires not involving people or property
limitations: the broad definition does not identify the exact location or environmental impact of an incident

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Chimney-fire classification definition
verified_claims: chimney fires are fires in non-industrial buildings where the flame is contained within the chimney structure
limitations: the category does not describe building compliance or condition

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Annual fire-count change
verified_claims: 170,597 fires were attended in the year ending March 2026, 19% more than the previous year
limitations: year-on-year fire counts are weather-sensitive and should not be extrapolated to an individual property

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Primary-fire annual count
verified_claims: 66,383 primary fires were attended in the year ending March 2026
limitations: the national primary-fire count does not identify a local hazard
